result.title: Fast-Slow Evolutionary Occupancy Prediction via Controlled Dynamics
result.summary: 3D semantic occupancy prediction provides dense geometric and semantic scene representations for autonomous driving, where both high accuracy and low response latency are crucial for safe downstream forecasting and planning. Existing methods usually exhibit different accuracy-latency characteristics. Performance-oriented models provide stronger geometric and semantic predictions, while deployment-friendly models provide faster responses. This motivates EvoOcc, a fast-slow evolutionary occupancy prediction framework that jointly exploits their complementary strengths to improve the accuracy-latency balance without changing the upstream architectures. EvoOcc models evolutionary occupancy prediction as a continuous time controlled dynamical system, enabling flexible adaptation to variable slow system delays and irregular fast system arrivals. The framework further decomposes the evolution process into dual state evolution where ego state evolution compensates for the deterministic coordinate shifts and scene state evolution models the genuine geometric and semantic scene changes. Extensive experiments on three different fast-slow system pairs and irregular prediction arrivals show that EvoOcc consistently improves over fast system baselines while maintaining much lower latency than the slow system, indicating a favorable accuracy-latency balance and stable behavior under practical inference situations.

AI.brief_summary: EvoOcc 面向自动驾驶 3D 语义占据预测，把快-慢两套系统的输出融合建模为连续时间受控动力系统，并将状态演化拆分为补偿坐标平移的 ego 状态与刻画真实场景变化的状态，以适应慢系统延迟与快系统不规则到达，在不改动上游架构的前提下改善精度-时延平衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其连续时间状态演化与快-慢双状态分解，可供核查如何把 latent 推理状态的更新建模为受控动力学，并在计算预算或证据到达不规则时异步更新状态；但论文关注占据预测而非 VLM 推理，迁移属推测。
